transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been thinking about death a lot lately, and wondering if my family would be better off without me. My daughter got really worried when I mentioned it to her, so she brought me in to get some help. It's just been really hard to carry this around.
Have you experienced these feelings of sadness or hopelessness before, or is this the first time in your life you have felt this way?

No, it's not the first time, but these heavy, hopeless feelings and mood swings have been coming and going for about a year now. It really started ramping up around the time my husband and I began discussing my retirement and I started cutting back my work hours.

Over the past several years, have there been periods of at least two months where you felt relatively 'normal' or back to your usual self, or has this low mood been present most days for the entire year?

No, I really haven't had any periods where I felt normal. This heavy, hopeless feeling has been hanging over me pretty steadily for the entire year, ever since my husband and I first started talking seriously about my retirement.
During this past year, have you experienced any brief periods of feeling significantly worse, or has the intensity of your low mood and hopelessness remained relatively constant?

It has been very constant, like a heavy cloud that just won't lift. I haven't really had brief spikes of feeling worse; it has just been a steady, flat hopelessness day after day since we started planning my retirement.
Over this past year of feeling low, have you noticed consistent changes in your sleep, appetite, or your ability to concentrate on daily tasks?

My appetite is almost completely gone—I mostly survive on coffee, my clothes are getting loose, and my mind feels incredibly foggy. I can't even focus enough to read a page in a book or decide what to make for breakfast. Sleep hasn't really been the main issue during these low periods, though.

Over this past year, have there been any specific two-week periods where your symptoms, such as the loss of appetite and inability to concentrate, became so severe that they significantly impaired your ability to function compared to how you feel on a 'typical' day?

No, it hasn't been just in two-week blocks—these severe symptoms have been hanging over me steadily for the entire year. It has completely disrupted my life because I've had to stop managing my properties, pull out of my book club, and rely on my husband to handle the cooking and bills.
Looking back further than this past year, have you ever experienced similar periods of feeling this low, hopeless, and unable to function at any point in your earlier life?

No, I haven't really experienced periods of feeling this low or unable to function before this past year. These severe feelings and swings only really started ramping up once my husband and I began discussing my retirement.
Before this past year, have you ever had any other periods in your life, perhaps lasting several weeks or months, where you felt depressed, lost interest in things, or felt unable to function?

No, I don't recall ever having periods of depression or losing interest in things like this before this past year. This level of struggle feels completely new to me, and it seems really tied to starting my retirement.
